narration.text: For millions of years, when the sun went down, the day was simply over.
Then someone, somewhere, learned to keep a fire alive.
We don't know who, or when. The oldest traces we can be reasonably sure of lie in a cave in southern Africa: ash, and burnt bone, about a million years old.
Fire meant warmth, cooked food, and some safety from whatever was out there in the dark.
And for the first time, the day did not end when the sun did.
